Public Participation Information

  participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 872 5896 3082, Meeting Password: 339794. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &

  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 872 5896 3082, Meeting Password: 339794. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following

  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  MARCH 28, 2022

CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:02 P.M. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.

SALUTE TO THE FLAG

PRESENTATION
CHAIR SCHMITZ introduced herself as the new Chair of the Equestrian Committee.

ROLL CALL
Committee Members Present:  Schmitz, Brtis, Griggs, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano,
  Robinson, Harik, Schachter
Committee Members Absent:  Ciarolla, Martin
City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor, Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
MEMBER ROBINSON moved seconded by MEMBER HARIK to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE NOVEMBER 29, 2021, SPECIAL
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AND THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE
  JANUARY 24, 2022, REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES AS
  PRESENTED.
CHAIR SCHMITZ abstained from the vote.
There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.
AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
None.
STAFF ITEMS
A. REQUEST TO PROVIDE EQUINE ASSISTED TALK THERAPY AT CITY FACILITIES

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 28, 2022
  1
 Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
MEMBER SHINN asked if the operation would involve two people on foot with one
horse walking around the trails and arenas. Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed. MEMBER
SHINN stated she was concerned that Chandler Arena is too small for the proposed
operation considering the lessons that take place there and stated other arenas, such
as those at Ernie Howlett Park and trails would be good for the operation, but expressed
that the operation is a wonderful service.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked if Ms. Gragg would need to follow the same parameters
required for other trainers. Ms. Gragg affirmed she would follow the same rules.
Supervisor Pinuelas stated the restriction for consecutive lessons would also be
followed.

CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that she appreciated this solution for mental health and that
this was a wonderful way to demonstrate support of the equestrian the community.
CHAIR SCHMITZ asked why Chandler Arena was identified for this use being that it can
get congested. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that Chandler Arena has been
requested because of its proximity to the Peter Weber Equestrian Center, which is
where the horse that will be used is boarded.

MEMBER SILVANO shared that she thought it was a great idea and that she
considered Pepperwood to be the ideal spot if someone was not already in the round
pen. She added that the operation would have to follow the established rules.

Community Member Pam Schachter stated that the maximum time allowed in the
Pepperwood pen is 20 minutes. She stated her concern related to the use of Chandler
Park because of the current difficulty to share the ring. She added that she supports the
use of Pepperwood, unless Chandler is not being used, but would not recommend the
use of the Chandler Arena.

Ms. Gragg stated that her current practice is about being creative and flexible with the
space available and that she doesn’t need a set space to work in. She added that if she
needed a contained space, the Pepperwood round pen is preferable to her and that she
understands Chandler Arena can be busy. Ms. Gragg added that the horse she works
with is not comfortable with the Ernie Howlett trail and arenas so she would stick with
the nearby trails and Pepperwood round pen, using Chandler if needed.

MEMBER NIELSEN asked if therapy would also be provided on trails and the open
landfill loop and if so, how much time would be spent on the trails versus the rings. Ms.
Gragg responded that she would use the trails or the landfill loop, depending on the day
and situation. She would see if the spaces were occupied or after checking in with the
client, may decide to work in the stall as needed, adding the need to be flexible.

MEMBER NIELSEN asked if therapy appointments normally occur at the same time as
peak riding times on weekends or is it during regular business hours. Ms. Gragg

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 28, 2022
  2
 responded that they will not take place on weekends, adding that appointments would
take place on Mondays, Tuesdays, or Wednesdays during business hours, sometimes
extending into early evening during daylight hours.

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER NIELSEN, TO APPROVE AS
FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECOMMEND FOR ADMISTRATIVE APPROVAL THE LICENSE WITH THE
  PERMIT CONDITIONS AS PRESENTED

AYES:  Brits, Griggs, Nielsen, Silvano, Robinson, Schacter, Schmitz
NOES:  Shinn
ABSENT:  Martin

The motion carried.
B. REQUEST TO PROVIDE WESTERN RIDING BARRELS IN ARENAS
Superintendent Goldsmith provided a verbal overview per written report.

CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if the recommendation was to not install permanent barrels.
Superintendent Goldsmith responded that permanent barrels would not be moved and
that running around a barrel over and over causes wear and tear, whereas mobile
barrels would be placed in different spots.

MEMBER SHINN asked if there was a maintenance issue when barrels were there
previously. She added that she saw barrels at Empty Saddle which were easy to move
and can be left outside the arena. She added that since it would be for amateur use, it
likely would not be used often.

Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the City is aware of one person had asked about
western barrels and that another individual purchased portable barrels. In response to
MEMBER SHINN, he explained that there were constant problems with footing when
barrels were placed previously.

MEMBER HARIK asked for clarification regarding the type of mobile barrels to be used.

Superintendent Goldsmith shared that he explored the idea with trainers in the
community (Fitzpatricks, Jan Ball, and Sean Martin) who concurred that permanent
barrels may not be needed at City arenas, and it would increase maintenance needs.
Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he does not think there will be fast people using
them but even with use by youth, there would still be a need to increase the frequency
in arena maintenance.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 28, 2022
  3
 CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if the Committee wished to entertain a motion to deny
purchasing permanent or temporary barrels and their placement; but would not preclude
individuals from setting up their own temporary and mobile equipment.

MEMBER Harik agreed as temporary barrels would not affect the arena.

There being a consensus, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

C. EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS UPDATE

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal update, including information regarding the
Equine Herpesvirus (also known as EHM or EHV-1) detection and shared that caution
had been advised for equine events. She also shared that a horseshow scheduled for
March had been cancelled and that no horse shows were planned until June.

She added that the equine subcommittee met earlier that day and discussed the issue
and the emergency water cache project, their placement, guidelines and protocols for
the water caches.

MEMBER SILVANO stated there was an advisory to not let horses leave properties and
asked how we could be proactive and get info out when these advisories and instances
occur. ACM Davis responded that staff connected with LA County Animal Care and
when there is a direct impact to the local community messaging would be shared
through RHE Alert Equestrian notifications and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horsemens
Association; however, staff would connect to learn how to get advance notice of similar
situations through the State agencies.

MEMBER SILVANO asked if a procedural manual for emergency response could be
created detailing how to get information and warnings out to the community. She also
asked which agency has the highest rank for protocols to be followed.

CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to create a protocol for communication to be followed
when emergencies such as that created by the EHV-1 virus occur.

D. CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT LIST

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the report.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked about the amount of available funding. CHAIR SCHMITZ
responded that the amount depends on what funds or grants are available adding that
year over year funds are allocated for projects as identified and prioritized.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked about the Perimeter Pathway project. MEMBER HARIK
asked about the Butcher Park project. ACM Davis provided a brief overview of both
projects.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 28, 2022
  4
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

E. CHANDLER PLAYGROUND SURVEY (VERBAL REPORT)

ACM Davis shared that the results of the survey would be presented to the April Park
and Activities Commission meeting.

F. MAYOR'S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief update stating that the event would take place on
May 21, 2022. CHAIR SCHMITZ encouraged the Committee to attend the event.

G. HORSE TRAINER BUSINESS LICENSE 2022 UPDATE

Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal update stating that a total 19 licenses had been
processed to date and that updated lists would be posted and updates would be made
as renewals get completed.

H. EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

MEMBER GRIGGS commented on the Ferncreek residential trail stating that a pathway
was being put in and inquiring about the rules. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he
was aware of a path on the upper slope, and that Code Enforcement and Planning
Department staff had assessed the area and determined it was permitted.

MEMBER NIELSEN noted she saw the same and had not noticed any more grading
work since the original concerns were presented.

MEMBER GRIGGS thanked Superintendent Goldsmith for work done to clear a tree
that had fallen. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that many times staff isn’t aware
of issues as they occur, and that staff appreciates when the public reaches out and
shares what they see.

MEMBER SHINN stated that she witnessed some younger gentleman flying drones at
the landfill. MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the restriction of drone deliveries would be
explored in the future for companies expressing safety concerns with regards to horses.

CHAIR SCHMITZ directed staff to add the item to the action list for further exploration.

MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the traffic committee could consider putting in crosswalk
lights, similar to those at City Hall, on Hawthorne Blvd and PV Drive North. She shared
that she witnessed an issue when two horses crossed legally but a driver stopped
suddenly and proceeded to honk at the rider which excited the horses. MEMBER
HARIK stated that type of situation can’t always be controlled but that traffic lights
should help. MEMBER SHINN added that riders should go through a trail instead of

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
MARCH 28, 2022
  5
 crossing Hawthorne Blvd. MEMBER GRIGGS responded they were crossing
Hawthorne Blvd having no access to tunnel. MEMBER BRTIS stated there are a lot of
concerns with drivers and equestrians.

CHAIR SCHMITZ shared that she also saw a concern with drivers and recommended
the use of social media to provide friendly reminders with regards to the issue,
reminding the community to be patient and allow other community members to safely
cross the streets.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

A. ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

MEMBER HARIK AND CHAIR SCHMITZ commented on the impacts caused the rain.
Staff was requested to continue to monitor situations as they occur.

B. MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

None.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  CHANDLER ARENA HORSE FACILITY IMPROVEMENTS
B.  UPDATE TRAIL RIDING PERMIT CATEGORY
C.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM
D.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION

Supervisor Pinuelas noted that staff would be bringing the future agenda items back to
the Committee soon.

CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting 8:07 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

Rosa Pinuelas  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
Community Services Supervisor
